description:
If you don't know who Peppa Pig is.....i'm sure your kid does!

In todays video, I use a super cheap popsicle mould in the glory of Peppa Pig to make super LOW SUGAR ice pops. The total Calories per 100g is only 126kcal, thats 38kcal per popsicle!! 👍👍

You don't have to have kids to make these, just maybe use a different mould 😉😂

The recipe is in the video, fresh, creamy ice pops for anyone. Enjoy in the summer sun!

-------------------

Not interested in Popsicles? Check out this amazing Blueberry ice cream with marshmallow swirl: https://youtu.be/z1T75sEi0Ys?si=9tkX_OrzxDFZInCx

comments.text: Hello, thanks so much for your videos, extremely interessant. I am desperate to succeed on a keto ice cream and gelato, i found out that the best sweetener is allulose, unfortunately here in europe its still not approved by the FDA so i have no other choice but  to use powdered erythritol. I would appreciate so much if you share a recipe of vanilla base ice cream and gelato using 100 % powdered eryhtritol as sweetner . Man Many Thanks
comments.author: @benzakou

comments.text:
You cannot use 100% erythritol. That’s why no commercial recipes use it as the main source of sweetener. That’s also why anyone online who say you can are full of it…… 💩 
You can buy xylitol everywhere in the EU, that’s a MUCH better option for sugar free ice cream. You can use part erythritol but only around 30% of the sweetener and I discuss this in an upcoming video.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  even with LBG / guar Gum/ carregaanan , using 100 % powdered erythhritol wpuldnt work,?
comments.author: @benzakou

comments.text: Two very different ingredients. One is sugar, freezing point depression and solids, the others are stabilizers!
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery

comments.text: @PolarIceCreamery  i lean using a combination of stabilizers plus the erythritol as sweeetner wouldnt work?
comments.author: @benzakou

comments.text: I it won’t. You can only use 20% of the required solids when using erythritol due its effect on freezing. That leaves your recipe extremely short on total essential solids. You need solids then, not more stabilizers. You’ll end up with a dry mix, made of ice crystals that will get worse as  time goes on.
comments.author: @PolarIceCreamery
